text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The edit is correct. can_pass(road_id, vehicle, network=None) exists in logistics/access.py with exactly that signature, so the import and per-road checks work. best_route, routes_between, sites_served, and trips_needed are preserved verbatim. passable_route filters routes to those where truck or van may use every road (using r['roads'], not r['id']), picks the min by (km, id) matching best_route's ordering, and returns truck if a truck can use every road on the chosen route else van — verified against data/network.json (e.g. RT-06 via restricted R-09 yields van; RT-08 via open roads yields truck). rerouted_sites compares route ids between best_route and passable_route per distinct (from, to) pair, so a vehicle-only change (e.g. SITE-NVL-B where both pick RT-02, truck vs van) does not count, while genuine reroutes (SITE-CPL-B: RT-05 blocked by R-08 → RT-06; SITE-HGL-A: RT-07 blocked by R-12 → RT-08) do, and it returns sorted unique site names matching the sites_served convention. Routes with no usable vehicle (none here, but RT-05 today) correctly yield None and are not counted as rerouted."}}
reasoning:
Check the proposed edit against the code.

can_pass exists in logistics/access.py with signature (road_id, vehicle, network=None). Good.

Proposed routes.py: imports can_pass, load_network from logistics.access — both exist. Keeps routes_between, best_route unchanged, sites_served, trips_needed unchanged. Adds _usable, passable_route, rerouted_sites.

passable_route: resolves network, filters usable routes, picks min by (km, id), returns (route, _usable(route, network)). Since route is usable, _usable returns truck or van. Correct: truck if truck can use every road, else van. Matches ticket.

rerouted_sites: iterates distinct (from, to) pairs, compares best_route and passable_route route ids. Ticket says "the vehicle alone changing does not count" — comparing route ids handles that. Returns sorted unique site names. Ticket says "in name order" — sorted() gives alphabetical order, same as sites_served convention. Good.

Edge: passable_route returns None if no usable route — then site not counted as rerouted. Ticket says "for which passable_route finds a route that is different from the route best_route picks" — if passable_route returns None, no route found, so not counted. Correct.

One subtlety: rerouted_sites iterates all (from,to) pairs in network['routes'], not just sites served by a warehouse — but that's what the plan says (R3: each distinct pair). Fine.

Check data: e.g., SITE-NVL-B: best_route picks RT-02 (22km, roads R-01 A, R-03 R) — truck can't use R-03, van can. So passable_route returns (RT-02, van) — same route, vehicle-only change, not rerouted. Correct per ticket.

SITE-CPL-B: RT-05 has R-08 (X) — unusable. RT-06 (26km, R-07 A, R-09 R) — van only. passable_route returns (RT-06, van), best is RT-05 — different route, rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-A: RT-07 has R-12 (X) — unusable. RT-08 (27km, R-10 A, R-11 A) — truck. passable returns (RT-08, truck). Rerouted. Good.

SITE-HGL-B: RT-09 has R-13 (R) — van only, same route, not rerouted. Good.

Everything checks out. The edit preserves existing functions verbatim. Accept.
